html:
Performers
BBC Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Ralph Vaughan Williams (conductor) Documented

Both the Archive item and the EMI reissue notes credit the composer as conductor. Individual players are not identified.

[1] [3]
Work version
Complete first movement of the orchestral symphony Inferred, not documented

The Archive item lists the four movements and splits the set into three files without saying which file holds which movement. The first file runs 8 min 2 s and ends in a quiet close that matches Hyperion’s description of the first movement’s pianissimo coda.

[1] [4]
Recorded
1937-10-11 Documented

The Archive item writes the date as 11-10-1937; the EMI reissue notes give 11th October 1937.

[1] [3]
Place
No. 1 Studio, Abbey Road, London Documented

The EMI reissue notes name No. 1 Studio, Abbey Road; BBC Music Magazine places the session in Abbey Road Studio 1.

[3] [5]
Label
HMV (The Gramophone Company) Documented

Twelve-inch 78-rpm records.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
HMV DB 8406–⁠9 or DB 3367–⁠3370 Disputed: sources disagree

The Archive item catalogues the set as DB 8406–⁠9 (automatic coupling); the EMI reissue notes give DB 3367–⁠3370 as the original 78s. They probably label the same performances in two side sequences, but that is not established here.

  • DB 8406–⁠9 (automatic coupling)
  • DB 3367–⁠3370
[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Matrices 2EA 5400 (take 2), 5801 (2), 5802 (1A), 5803 (2A), 5804 (1), 5805 (2A), 5806 (1A), 5807 (1A): eight sides Documented

The Archive description lists the takes; the EMI notes list the same matrix numbers. Which sides make up the first file is not stated.

[1] [3]
Transfer
Internet Archive “Satyr 78rpm” collection Documented

The item is filed in that collection; no transfer engineer is named in the description.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Archive upload date (13 May 2018) is not a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
FLAC, Ogg Vorbis and variable-bitrate MP3 derivatives, in three segments (a first file, a second, and a third joining the remaining two discs). Documented

Equalisation, speed correction and noise reduction are not documented.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Vaughan Williams’s copyright in the music runs to the end of 2028 in the UK and EU. Documented

The Vaughan Williams Foundation gives 2028 as the year copyright in his music expires. Composition rights are separate from the recording.

[6]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial issue in 1938, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The EMI reissue notes date the original HMV 78s “℗ 1938”. The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule then applies: the former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is not United States or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

[1] [3] [7]

Ralph Vaughan Williams, Symphony No. 4, I. Allegro; BBC Symphony Orchestra, Ralph Vaughan Williams. HMV DB 8406–⁠9 (first issued 1938), Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Vaughan Williams’s copyright subsists in the UK and EU until the end of 2028.

  2. Internet Archive — file inventory for the Symphony No. 4 item — Vaughan Williams Symf 4 HMV DB8406-9 1.mp3 (first file, 8 min 2 s), with FLAC and Ogg Vorbis derivatives; files 2 and 3-4 follow.. Accessed 2026-10-18.

HMV DB 3367–⁠3370; ℗ 1938. Liner notes by Michael Kennedy.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  4. Hyperion Records — Vaughan Williams: Symphonies Nos 3 & 4, booklet note by Robert Matthew-⁠Walker (CDA68280) — Description of the Fourth Symphony’s opening, four-note figure, contrapuntal treatment, first-movement coda, première of 10 April 1935 and dedication to Bax.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  5. BBC Music Magazine (classical-music.com) — The best recordings of Vaughan Williams Symphony No. 4 — Entry for the 1937 BBC Symphony Orchestra recording under the composer: Abbey Road Studio 1, October 1937; Naxos Historical 8.111048.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
